key_insight: Intra-patient 3D multimodal deformable registration remains unsolved across anatomies and modalities, with strong dataset dependence and a persistent mismatch between overlap-based and image-consistency metrics.
engineering_relevance: For clinical registration pipelines, this means method selection must be anatomy- and modality-specific and validated with multiple criteria, not just segmentation overlap.
method: Benchmarked classical optimization-based and modern learning-based registration methods, including recent deep and foundation models.
Evaluated performance on three datasets spanning synthetic deformation recovery and real clinical scenarios.
Used complementary metrics: DSC, HD95, and MIND-SSC to capture geometric and structural correspondence.
evidence_signal: Across three datasets, learning-based methods performed best on large synthetic benchmarks, but gains were limited in real pelvic registration and metric disagreement was common.
watch_item: Anatomy-guided methods can inflate overlap scores while degrading global alignment outside segmented regions, so relying on label-driven metrics alone may be misleading.
paper_title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration
